declarations.name: pP
declarations.doc: /-- Vertex `i` of `P`, as an index into the fourteen. -/
declarations.text: def pP (i : Fin 7) : Fin 14 := ⟨i.val, by omega⟩

declarations.name: pQ
declarations.doc: /-- Vertex `i` of `Q`, as an index into the fourteen. -/
declarations.text: def pQ (i : Fin 7) : Fin 14 := ⟨7 + i.val, by omega⟩

declarations.name: SimpleClosed
declarations.doc:
/-- Simplicity of a closed heptagon **as a curve**, and nothing else: no
degenerate side, non-adjacent sides disjoint, and cyclically adjacent sides
meeting exactly in their shared endpoint.

Three collinear vertices are **allowed** — that is the entire point.  Contrast
`DisjointnessGraph.Simple7`, whose second conjunct is already a general-position
condition, and `Config`, whose `no_*_vertex_on_*_side_line` fields already
assume away half of what §9 exists to remove.  Neither can be the source of a
reduction whose job is to create those conditions. -/
declarations.text:
def SimpleClosed (W : Fin 7 → ℝ × ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Fin 7, W i ≠ W (i + 1)) ∧
  (∀ i j : Fin 7, ¬ LowerBound.Adjacent i j →
      Disjoint (segment ℝ (W i) (W (i + 1))) (segment ℝ (W j) (W (j + 1)))) ∧
  (∀ i : Fin 7,
      segment ℝ (W i) (W (i + 1)) ∩ segment ℝ (W (i + 1)) (W (i + 2))
        = {W (i + 1)})

declarations.name: Pair9
declarations.doc:
/-- Two heptagons in the real plane, each simple as a point set.  **No general
position of any kind.** -/
declarations.text:
structure Pair9 where
  /-- The fourteen vertices: `P` is `0..6`, `Q` is `7..13`. -/
  V : Fin 14 → ℝ × ℝ
  simpleP : SimpleClosed (fun i : Fin 7 => V (pP i))
  simpleQ : SimpleClosed (fun i : Fin 7 => V (pQ i))

declarations.name: NoVertexOnOther
declarations.doc:
/-- **(E9).** No vertex of either polygon lies anywhere on the other polygon's
boundary.  This is what AKR §9 delivers — §9.1 removes vertex–vertex
coincidences, §9.2 vertex–side ones — and it is imported, not proved.

Both directions are used: the `P`-vertices to place an intersection point
strictly inside a `Q`-side, and the `Q`-vertices to rule out a collinear
overlap. -/

declarations.name: sideP9
declarations.text:
def sideP9 (R : Pair9) (i : Fin 7) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  segment ℝ (R.V (pP i)) (R.V (pP (i + 1)))

declarations.name: sideQ9
declarations.text:
def sideQ9 (R : Pair9) (j : Fin 7) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  segment ℝ (R.V (pQ j)) (R.V (pQ (j + 1)))

declarations.name: bdryP9
declarations.text: def bdryP9 (R : Pair9) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := ⋃ i : Fin 7, sideP9 R i

declarations.name: bdryQ9
declarations.text: def bdryQ9 (R : Pair9) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := ⋃ j : Fin 7, sideQ9 R j

declarations.name: points9
declarations.doc: /-- `∂P ∩ ∂Q`, a genuine set of points of the real plane. -/
declarations.text: def points9 (R : Pair9) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := bdryP9 R ∩ bdryQ9 R

declarations.name: attainedCoincFree
declarations.doc: /-- The attainable counts, under finiteness and coincidence-freeness only. -/

declarations.name: points9_le_38_of_coincFree
declarations.doc:
/-- **§9.2's half of `(A9)`, unconditionally.**

If the two boundaries meet in finitely many points and the two heptagons
**share no vertex**, then they meet in at most `38` points.

The vertex-on-**side** degeneracies — the ones AKR §9.2 removes by shifting —
are handled here in full: the chain of tilted shifts terminates, the joint
measure `crossPairs + segDeg + segDegP` never falls, and the endpoint has no
degeneracies, where the measure is just the crossing count and `≤ 38` is the
project's own bound for two simple heptagons.

**This is not `f(7,7) = 38`, and it is not all of AKR §9.** The hypothesis
`hcoinc` — no shared vertex — is §9.**1**'s conclusion, and it is assumed here,
not proved. `AKR9.NoVertexOnOther` remains a hypothesis of the main
development, and `f(7,7) = 38` remains conditional on the §9 import. Nothing
here has been reviewed by a mathematician. -/
declarations.text:
theorem points9_le_38_of_coincFree (R : Pair9) (hfin : (points9 R).Finite)
    (hcoinc : ∀ v j : Fin 7, R.V (pP v) ≠ R.V (pQ j)) :
    (points9 R).ncard ≤ 38 := by
  obtain ⟨Rend, hD, hE, hb⟩ := exists_chain_deg_free _ R hfin hcoinc rfl
  exact points9_le_38_of_joint R Rend hfin hb hD hE

declarations.name: isGreatest_38_of_coincFree
declarations.doc:
/-- **38 is the greatest attainable count, assuming only `(Fin)` and that the
two heptagons share no vertex.**

Strictly weaker than `AKR9.isGreatest_38_of_E9`, whose hypothesis (E9) forbids
a vertex anywhere on the other boundary.  **This is still not `f(7,7) = 38`:**
coincidence-freeness is §9.1's conclusion and is assumed, not proved. -/
declarations.text:
theorem isGreatest_38_of_coincFree : IsGreatest attainedCoincFree 38 := by
  refine ⟨⟨AKR9.certPair9, certPair9_finite, certPair9_coincFree,
    AKR9.certPair9_ncard⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro n ⟨R, hfin, hco, rfl⟩
  exact points9_le_38_of_coincFree R hfin hco

declarations.name: nonVacuity
declarations.text:
theorem nonVacuity :
    Nonempty AKR9.Pair9
    ∧ (points9 AKR9.certPair9).Nonempty
    ∧ (points9 AKR9.certPair9).Finite
    ∧ (∀ v j : Fin 7, AKR9.certPair9.V (pP v) ≠ AKR9.certPair9.V (pQ j))
    ∧ AKR9.NoVertexOnOther AKR9.certPair9
    ∧ (points9 AKR9.certPair9).ncard = 38
    ∧ ¬ (points9 AKR9.certPair9).ncard ≤ 37
    ∧ (38 : ℕ) ∈ attainedCoincFree
    ∧ (39 : ℕ) ∉ attainedCoincFree
    ∧ IsGreatest attainedCoincFree 38 :=
  ⟨pair9_nonempty, certPair9_points9_nonempty, certPair9_finite,
   certPair9_coincFree, certPair9_noVertexOnOther, AKR9.certPair9_ncard,
   certPair9_not_le_37, mem_attainedCoincFree_38, not_mem_attainedCoincFree_39,
   isGreatest_38_of_coincFree⟩

declarations.name: certPair9_not_le_37
declarations.doc:
/-- **(NV6) The bound is not slack.**  `≤ 38` is attained; `≤ 37` is false on
the very configuration the theorem applies to.  So the constant `38` is forced
and cannot be improved by a reader's inspection. -/
declarations.text:
theorem certPair9_not_le_37 : ¬ (points9 AKR9.certPair9).ncard ≤ 37 := by
  intro h
  rw [AKR9.certPair9_ncard] at h
  omega

declarations.name: isGreatest_attainedCoincFree_unique
declarations.doc:
/-- **(NV9) `IsGreatest` pins the value.**  Any greatest element of
`attainedCoincFree` equals `38`: the theorem does not merely assert an upper
bound, it identifies the maximum. -/
